prompt: Storybook painterly illustration, night, HIGH CONTRAST with deep true blacks. A MINIATURE VILLAGE BUILT BY CAT-SIZED CREATURES — the whole settlement is tiny, and its scale is shown by NATURE TOWERING OVER IT: fern fronds arch higher than the rooflines, blades of grass rise past the eaves, a fallen pine cone beside the lane is larger than a barrel, mushroom caps stand as tall as the doorways, moss grows like shrubbery, dewdrops are heavy and huge on the leaves. The buildings are small and beautifully made: charred black cedar siding, fresh pale milled timber, tiny corrugated roofs, deep eaves, dry-stacked pebble footings, small salvaged glass windows. LIMITED NIGHT PALETTE: near-black, deep indigo, slate, moss green; the ONLY saturated colour is warm amber light from the windows. No text, no lettering, no signage. A narrow lane between three tiny dwellings, seen from ground level among the grass stems. The creatures are present but rendered as PURE BLACK SILHOUETTES, strongly backlit by the warm light behind them — no facial features whatsoever, no visible detail, only shape and posture: one small rounded silhouette standing in a brightly lit doorway with the light blazing past it, one seated shape on a veranda rail in profile, and two tiny warm points of carried light far down the misty lane. Graphic, bold, shadow-puppet clarity.
